Initial Observations

The dataset comprises 11 variables and a total of 61,892 records. All column names consist solely of alphanumeric characters, begin with a lowercase letter, and use underscores to separate words.
Missing values exist in the runtime and views fields. This stems from inconsistencies in the raw data reported by Netflix, specific durations were not recorded for some titles, making it impossible to calculate the corresponding view counts. Missing records also appear in the release_date field, as this information was not always available.
Both hours_viewed and views exhibit extreme positive skewness, sparklines reveal that the data is heavily concentrated near the minimum value. For hours_viewed, 75% of the titles fall within the 6.4 million-hour range, yet the maximum value soars to 964,100,000 hours. Similarly, for views, 75% of the titles fall within 1.2 million views, while the maximum reaches 144,800,000 views.

Corporate Strategy Memo
MEMORANDUM
TO: Netflix Leadership
FROM: Content Strategy & Data Analytics
SUBJECT: Strategic Content for 2027 and Beyond

Executive Summary
This memo outlines strategic recommendations for Netflix’s content strategies for 2027 and beyond. Based on actual viewership data, investment should prioritize episodic series rather than movies. Live event should be used to drive new user sign-ups rather than to build overall watch time. Additionally, the platform must retain classic shows to prevent existing subscribers from cancelling their memberships after finishing new releases.


Data Insights

Episodic Series Drive the Core of Viewership

Episodic series are the primary drivers of platform viewership. Since data standardization began in the 2023H2, episodic series have consistently accounted for 94.75% to 96.47% of total watch time across the platform, while movies represent only 3.53% to 5.25% of the share. Since a single season of a series comprises multiple episodes, viewers often binge-watch for hours on end, generating significantly more effective watch time than movies, which are typically completed in one or two hours.

Catalog Expansion and Classic Series

Netflix’s catalog has grown steadily, which expanding from 6,574 titles (50,117 total hours) in the 2023H2 to 8,163 titles (62,855 total hours) in the 2026H1, an increase of 24.2% in title count and 25.4% in total duration. Beyond the new blockbuster hits released periodically, the platform relies heavily on classic shows. For example, Pablo Escobar, el patron del mal: Season 1 has generated over 105,500,000 hours of viewership within the recorded periods, despite having premiered years ago. These classic shows are crucial for retaining the audience during gaps between major new releases.

The Vast Gap Between Live Event and Pre-taped

While live event generates significant buzz and conversation on social media, the data reveals that most of the viewership remains concentrated on standard pre-taped. On average, pre-taped garners approximately 8,289,547 hours of viewing time, while live event average less than 3,560,000 hours, which means pre-taped generates more than 2.3 times the viewership of live event. The disparity is even more striking when comparing top-performing hits, the most popular pre-taped show reached 964,100,000 hours for a single installment, while the most popular live event garnered only 235,700,000 hours. Once the day of the live event passes, few viewers revisit the replay, unlike standard series, live event cannot accumulate viewing hours over the long term.


Strategic Recommendations for 2027 and Beyond

Primary investment toward episodic series IPs

Reduce investment in standalone movies, which often have moderate costs but lose relevance after a single viewing. Therefore, we should concentrate the budget on multi-season shows, as episodic series account for approximately 95% of total platform viewership.

Treat live event as sign-up drivers rather than watch-time engines

The primary objective of live event should be to attract new viewers who do not typically watch Netflix, encouraging them to subscribe on event day. We should avoid spending money on small, low-profile live event shows. Instead, invest only in a select few marquee events that draw a massive global audience.

Secure long-term licensing for classic shows with high guaranteed viewership

Maintain reliable licensing agreements for multi-episode comfort staples with guaranteed viewership floors. These shows keep subscribers engaged daily between flagship releases, directly minimizing subscription cancellations.







NoteAI Usage Statement





Gemini was used to help troubleshoot R code, specifically for using vectorized if_else( ) instead of standard if…else statements to categorize data, and gt( ) part. Additionally, it was used to provide background context and brainstorm ideas for the open-ended prompt. All non-code text and analytical interpretations were written without generative AI.

title: Mini-Project #02
text:
Data Analysis

Task 5: Calculate Total Emissions per Agency-Mode Pair


Show code
# Add up trips and passenger miles for each agency-mode pair
service_clean <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  mutate(NTD_ID = as.character(NTD_ID)) |>
  group_by(NTD_ID, mode, AGENCY, state) |>
  summarize(
    total_upt = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum_passenger_miles = sum(sum_passenger_miles),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Combine service, energy, and EIA state emission table
transit_emissions <- service_clean |>
  inner_join(NTD_ENERGY |> mutate(`NTD ID` = as.character(`NTD ID`)), by = c("NTD_ID" = "NTD ID", "mode" = "Mode")) |>
  left_join(select(EIA_SEP_REPORT, abbreviation, CO2_MWh), by = c("state" = "abbreviation")) |>
  mutate(
    # CO2 estimates in pounds, using published factors and stated approximations
    co2_diesel    = coalesce(`Gallons of Diesel Fuel`, 0) * 22.45,
    co2_biodiesel = coalesce(`Gallons of Bio-Diesel`, 0) * 22.45,
    co2_gasoline  = coalesce(`Gallons of Gasoline`, 0) * 18.73,
    co2_cng = coalesce(`Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas`, 0) * (0.138 * 116.65),
    co2_lng = coalesce(`Gallons of Liquified Nat Gas`, 0) * (0.08482 * 116.65),
    co2_lpg       = coalesce(`Gallons of Liquified Petroleum Gas`, 0) * 12.68,
    co2_kerosene  = coalesce(`Gallons of Kerosene`, 0) * 21.78,
    co2_ethanol = coalesce(`Gallons of Ethanol`, 0) * (5.75 * 2.20462),
    co2_bunker    = coalesce(`Gallons of Bunker Fuel`, 0) * 24.78,
    
    # Grid electricity emissions: (kWh / 1000) * lbs CO2 per MWh
    electricity_kwh = coalesce(`Kilowatt hours of Electric Battery`, 0) +
                  coalesce(`Kilowatt hours of Electric Propulsion`, 0),

    co2_electric = if_else(
      electricity_kwh == 0,
      0,
      electricity_kwh / 1000 * CO2_MWh
    ),
    
    # Total emissions and emission intensity metrics
    total_co2_lbs = co2_diesel + co2_biodiesel + co2_gasoline + 
                    co2_cng + co2_lng + co2_lpg + co2_kerosene + 
                    co2_ethanol + co2_bunker + co2_electric,
    co2_per_passenger_mile = if_else(sum_passenger_miles > 0, total_co2_lbs / sum_passenger_miles, NA_real_),
    co2_per_upt            = if_else(total_upt > 0, total_co2_lbs / total_upt, NA_real_)
  )


Biodiesel, LPG, and bunker fuel use diesel, propane, and residual fuel oil as proxies. CNG assumes diesel gallon equivalents; LNG assumes 84,820 Btu/gallon. Ethanol includes biogenic CO2.

  ) |>

Task 6: Normalize Emissions to Transit Usage and Identify Efficient Agencies


Show code
# Sum emissions and transit usage across modes for each agency
agency_emissions <- transit_emissions |>
  group_by(NTD_ID, AGENCY, state) |>
  summarize(
    total_co2_lbs = sum(total_co2_lbs),
    total_upt = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum_passenger_miles = sum(sum_passenger_miles),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(
    total_upt >= 100000,
    sum_passenger_miles > 0,
    !is.na(total_co2_lbs),
    total_co2_lbs >= 0
  ) |>
  mutate(
    co2_per_passenger_mile = total_co2_lbs / sum_passenger_miles,
    co2_per_upt = total_co2_lbs / total_upt
  )

Task 8: Deliverable — Transit Award Press Release

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE: 2026 Green Transit Awards
CalVans takes the Greenest Transit Agency award in this year’s GTA IV analysis, while Plaquemines receives the Highest Emissions per Passenger Mile award.
Rankings use estimated CO2 emissions per passenger mile for agencies with at least 100,000 annual unlinked passenger trips. Agencies with missing emissions or no reported passenger miles were excluded.


Greenest Transit Agency: CalVans
CalVans wins with 0.139 lbs of CO2 per passenger mile, about 87.8% below the median of 1.135 lbs among the agencies compared.

Highest Emissions per Passenger Mile: Plaquemines
Plaquemines receives the Highest Emissions per Passenger Mile award, with 23.497 lbs of CO2 per passenger mile, about 20.7 times the median. Its average ferry trip was only 0.5 miles, which may help explain the high rate.
